answer: Behavioral Fingerprint Escrow: each identity locks a deposit. Its timing, wording, and partners form a print like the ridges on a fingertip. A velvet glove fits one hand; one print serves one identity. No copy can fake an opal's shifting colors or behavior. Peers audit each epoch; mismatch freezes the escrow, burns 30%. Faking 100 prints costs 100 x $40 = $4,000, yet fails audit. An honest agent pays once, keeps full reward.
